findings.evidence: Line 59 is exactly `ι_range_pow_le_filtration ... (k + 1) x.property`; `ι_range_pow_le_filtration` at Filtration.lean:265 is quantified over arbitrary `n`.
findings.fix: State it with `(n : ℕ) (x : ⋀[R]^n M)` and filtration degree `n`, then specialize it at `k + 1` downstream.
findings.issue: `exteriorPower_mem_zero_form_filtration` only handles degree `k + 1`, although its proof works unchanged for every `n : ℕ`.

findings.evidence: `equivExteriorFiltration Q k` at line 54 is defined for every `k`, and its inverse already maps the entire zero-form filtration step back to `filtration Q k`; lines 102–103 and 111–114 merely take `.property` of these unrestricted maps.
findings.fix: State the forward lemma for `(n) (x : filtration Q n)` and the inverse for `(n) (x : filtration (0 : QuadraticForm R M) n)`; construct the latter subtype from an exterior element only at the quotient call site.
findings.issue: Both new transport lemmas are under-generalized: the forward lemma unnecessarily uses `k + 1`, while the inverse lemma additionally accepts only `⋀[R]^(k + 1) M` instead of an arbitrary member of the zero-form filtration.

summary: The new membership API is unnecessarily restricted to successor degrees, and the inverse transport lemma is further restricted to exterior-power elements despite the underlying equivalence working on the whole filtration step.
